moments.selftext: A woman allegedly stole at least $4 billion, boarded a plane in 2017, and disappeared. Nearly a decade later, the FBI still hasn’t found her. Ruja Ignatova, known as the “Cryptoqueen,” vanished in 2017 after allegedly defrauding investors of billions through her fraudulent cryptocurrency, OneCoin. After learning that her American boyfriend was cooperating with the FBI, she flew from Sofia, Bulgaria, to Athens, Greece, and disappeared without a trace. She remains the only woman on the FBI’s Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list.

moments.selftext: A 1928 Thompson submachine gun concealed inside a violin case. The 1928 Thompson submachine gun hidden inside a violin case has become one of the most recognizable images associated with the Prohibition era. Hollywood and comic books popularized the idea of gangsters using instrument cases to conceal their weapons, although historical evidence suggests they were more likely to rely on ordinary luggage or canvas bags. Fitting a Thompson into a standard violin case required removing the wooden stock and positioning the weapon and magazines inside. The image became an enduring cultural symbol, blending the glamour of the Jazz Age with the violence of organized crime.
